The commuting-form construction theorem supplies division coefficients, triangular power identities, and a left-division-algebra basis of the full polynomial algebra.
The EGH manuscript claims the pure-powers Hilbert-function comparison in characteristic zero for regular sequences of every positive length.
The companion manuscript claims a single lex-plus-powers ideal with the same Hilbert function and all graded Betti numbers at least those of the given ideal, over every characteristic-zero field.
The low-relation induction yields the multiplicity-one-factor hypothesis required by the parameter theorem.
The assembly induction, using the division theorem, constructs all triangular identities and the full ordered basis.
The commuting-form construction implies the EGH Hilbert-function conclusion and its characteristic-zero extension.
The full commuting-form basis transfers resolutions and permits a Hilbert-matching monomial ideal with no smaller Betti numbers.

thm:parameters gives geometric integrality, the stated singular-codimension bound, smooth h-dimensional linear sections, and (M+2h)-connectivity of the smooth punctured cone.

The prescribed curve is a connected etale G-cover with a genuinely linearized degree-|G| line bundle, generic section rank |G|, a free Pic^1 action, and equivariant circle maps for all required characters.
The generic Morita module has rank e0*r and extends coherently with the associative Hom-line-corrected transport and commuting Delta0 action.
The determinant correction has universal-line scalar weights (-1,0), cancels the Morita transport cocycle, and gives genuine H-equivariance after derived restriction to R=0.
The mixed determinant line on B times P extracts the rank of every K-class pulled back from B, up to a fixed sign.
Pullback through a finite constant-group torsor of projective schemes multiplies the Euler characteristic of every coherent class by the torsor degree.
prop:rank-to-euler gives the genuine equivariant Delta0-module class beta with fiber index plus or minus r and twist indices chi/e0 in e0*e1*Z.
The cone connectivity and Pic^1 character maps give the equivariant projective test and the nonequivariant homotopies used to compare a smooth linear section.
Integration with the Todd class along a smooth projective variety over projective h-space is the Chern character of a unique integral K-class.
prop:index-test produces q_j in e1*Z with q_0=plus or minus r and all complete-intersection twist indices in e0*e1*Z.
For prime p, v>=1, ord_u(A mod p)=nu, h>=v*nu and AQ=0 modulo (p^v,u^(h+1)) imply p^v divides Q(0), including nu=0.
The complete-intersection Hilbert series and the exact prime-power truncation lemma force e0 to divide Q_*(0), hence e0*e1 divides every module's reduced rank.
The prescribed extension from F to K splits Delta1; this alone places no upper bound below e1 on ind_F(Delta1).

claims.natural_statement: Over any commutative ring R, let p in R, A,D,T,U,Q in R[X], and nu,v,h be natural numbers. If p^v=0, nu*v<=h, X^(h+1) divides A*Q, and X^nu=A*D+C(p)*T+X^(h+1)*U, then Q.coeff(0)=0. The source also proves the universal annihilator-power identity and determinant scalar weights (-1,0).

For prime p, if the polynomial A modulo p has exact order nu at zero, then for every h>=nu there are integer polynomials D,T,U with X^nu=A*D+p*T+X^(h+1)*U; a truncated inverse of the unit factor gives a deterministic construction.

import Mathlib.Algebra.Polynomial.Div
import Mathlib.RingTheory.Ideal.Quotient.Defs
import Mathlib.RingTheory.Ideal.Span
import Mathlib.Tactic.Ring
import Mathlib.Tactic.Omega

namespace DivisionIndexAudit

theorem power_mul_eq_of_mul_eq {R : Type*} [CommRing R]
    (s t q : R) (h : s * q = t * q) (n : Nat) :
    s ^ n * q = t ^ n * q := by
  induction n with
  | zero => simp
  | succ n ih =>
      calc
        s ^ (n + 1) * q = s * (s ^ n * q) := by rw [pow_succ]; ring
        _ = s * (t ^ n * q) := by rw [ih]
        _ = t ^ n * (s * q) := by ring
        _ = t ^ n * (t * q) := by rw [h]
        _ = t ^ (n + 1) * q := by rw [pow_succ]; ring

theorem nilpotent_lift {R : Type*} [CommRing R]
    (a d p c x q : R) (nu v : Nat)
    (ha : a * q = 0) (hx : x ^ nu = a * d + p * c)
    (hp : p ^ v = 0) :
    x ^ (nu * v) * q = 0 := by
  have hstep : x ^ nu * q = (p * c) * q := by
    calc
      x ^ nu * q = (a * q) * d + (p * c) * q := by rw [hx]; ring
      _ = (p * c) * q := by rw [ha]; simp
  calc
    x ^ (nu * v) * q = (x ^ nu) ^ v * q := by rw [pow_mul]
    _ = (p * c) ^ v * q := power_mul_eq_of_mul_eq _ _ _ hstep v
    _ = 0 := by rw [mul_pow, hp, zero_mul, zero_mul]

open Polynomial

theorem constant_zero_of_truncated_bezout {R : Type*} [CommRing R]
    (p : R) (A D T U Q : Polynomial R) (nu v h : Nat)
    (hp : p ^ v = 0) (hbound : nu * v <= h)
    (hAQ : X ^ (h + 1) ∣ A * Q)
    (hbezout : X ^ nu = A * D + C p * T + X ^ (h + 1) * U) :
    Q.coeff 0 = 0 := by
  let I : Ideal (Polynomial R) := Ideal.span {X ^ (h + 1)}
  let pi := Ideal.Quotient.mk I
  have hz : pi (X ^ (h + 1)) = 0 := by
    apply Ideal.Quotient.eq_zero_iff_mem.mpr
    exact Ideal.subset_span (by simp)
  have hz' : (pi X) ^ (h + 1) = 0 := by
    simpa only [map_pow] using hz
  have ha : pi A * pi Q = 0 := by
    rw [← map_mul]
    exact Ideal.Quotient.eq_zero_iff_mem.mpr
      (Ideal.mem_span_singleton.mpr hAQ)
  have hp' : (pi (C p)) ^ v = 0 := by
    simpa only [map_pow, map_zero] using
      congrArg (fun r : R => pi (C r)) hp
  have hx : (pi X) ^ nu = pi A * pi D + pi (C p) * pi T := by
    simpa only [map_pow, map_add, map_mul, hz', zero_mul, add_zero] using
      congrArg pi hbezout
  have hnil := nilpotent_lift (pi A) (pi D) (pi (C p)) (pi T)
    (pi X) (pi Q) nu v ha hx hp'
  have hmem : X ^ (nu * v) * Q ∈ I := by
    apply Ideal.Quotient.eq_zero_iff_mem.mp
    simpa only [map_mul, map_pow] using hnil
  have hdvd : X ^ (h + 1) ∣ X ^ (nu * v) * Q :=
    Ideal.mem_span_singleton.mp hmem
  have hcoeff := (Polynomial.X_pow_dvd_iff.mp hdvd)
    (nu * v) (by omega)
  simpa [Polynomial.coeff_X_pow_mul'] using hcoeff

theorem determinant_weights (g : Int) :
    (-(2 - g) + (1 - g), -(2 - g) + (2 - g)) = (-1, 0) := by
  apply Prod.ext <;> dsimp <;> ring

end DivisionIndexAudit

claims.natural_statement: The prescribed curve is a connected etale G-cover with a genuinely linearized degree-|G| line bundle, generic section rank |G|, a free Pic^1 action, and equivariant circle maps for all required characters.

external_assumptions.statement: The Abel map identifies invariant real one-forms on the Jacobian with harmonic real one-forms on the curve and induces an isomorphism on integral H1.
external_assumptions.source: Milne, Jacobian varieties, revised author version of 12 June 2021, Proposition 2.2 and Theorem 2.5.

external_assumptions.statement: For a line bundle M on a smooth connected projective complex curve of genus g, chi(M)=deg(M)+1-g; this is the curve specialization of algebraic Riemann-Roch.

claims.natural_statement: The generic Morita module has rank e0*r and extends coherently with the associative Hom-line-corrected transport and commuting Delta0 action.

external_assumptions.statement: For a finite Galois field extension, compatible semilinear vector-space descent is effective and fully faithful; multiplication and a unit descend as morphisms. Artins fixed-field theorem supplies the finite Galois extension from a faithful finite group of field automorphisms.
external_assumptions.source: Stacks Project, Lemma 35.6.1, Tag 0CDR, https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0CDR, read directly; Artins classical fixed-field theorem is a foundational algebraic input.
